newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan faces censure in foreign row.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan faces censure in foreign row.

text.p: A Turkish left-wing party said on Tuesday it had requested a parliamentary censure motion to topple Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for his Islamist foreign policy that has come under fire at home and abroad.
"Turkey is being damaged with every day that the government stays in power," MP Nihat Matkap of the Republican People's Party (CHP) told Reuters.
He said his party had asked parliament on Monday to take up the censure motion. MPs must debate it within two weeks.

The opposition and the Turkish media have slammed Erbakan for a visit to Libya at the weekend during which Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi strongly criticised Turkey's treatment of its Kurds and its ties to the West.
The United States has delivered what officials termed a "stiff rebuke" to NATO ally Turkey over the Libya visit.

Erbakan's Islamist-led coalition has five deputies more than the 276 needed to win a censure vote in the 550-seat assembly. But some members of the pro-Western True Path Party (DYP) government ally are uneasy at Erbakan's foreign efforts.
